gaps.sentence: Her eyes were red because she ___.
gaps.hint: visible result of an earlier activity
gaps.explanation: The past perfect continuous shows an activity whose results were visible at a past moment: had been crying.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.

gaps.sentence: When I was a boy, films ___ in black and white.
gaps.hint: a past state no longer existing
gaps.explanation: 'Used to be' describes a past state that has ended: used to be.

gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: He ___ about the situation, but he is pretending not to.
gaps.hint: know is never used in continuous forms
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so it takes the present simple: knows.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.
